scenario: An iPhone 13 owner wants two spare charging bricks, one for a bedroom and one for a travel bag. They are comparing a $5.99 generic 20 W PD brick, a $15.99 Anker 20 W brick, and a $22.99 UGREEN 65 W bundle. The frozen storefront ratings conflict with price and brand expectations, the listings make different protection claims, and forum posts recommend brands or describe a melted charger. The owner prioritizes verified electrical safety and exact phone-cable compatibility over ratings, brand, or headline wattage, and can keep using an undamaged known charger while better evidence is obtained.
target: Audit the three complete frozen charger listings, the two community discussions, and the generic AC-adapter, fuse, overheating, electrical-safety-standard, electrical-safety-testing, and USB-C evidence. Decide whether one exact model is established as the safest choice for two iPhone 13 spare locations or whether purchase must be deferred. Preserve exact price and rating displays, included and missing cables, output profiles, seller attribution, incident scope, jurisdiction and model-binding limits, stop-use gates, and every missing certification, test method, threshold, result, failure denominator, and compatibility check.
